text:
omar: FYI perf CI flagged a regression on release/v1.8 after yesterday's merge. throughput drop ~11% on long-ctx workloads.

sylvia: ugh. which merge? any kernel/quant change landed?

omar: the merge was #4821 (auto-kernel-selector tweaks + batching heuristic tweak).

cheng: I ran a quick local profile. KV cache hit rate looks the same, but there are ~2x more kernel-switch syscalls per step. suspect selector now prefers the fused attention path for mid-sized seqs — not always cheaper.

marta: ci-bot posted the perf run:
```
ci-bot: perf/regression v1.8-rc: throughput 78 tok/s (baseline 88 tok/s) -11.4%
trace id: perf-2026-03-18-08
build: 1.8.3-merge-4821
config: batch_size=8, seq=1024, kv_cache=true
```

anya: did the batching heuristic change? that can nudge kernel selection if we feed different micro-batches.

omar: yes, the heuristic now groups by request_size_estimate instead of seq_length_bucket. intended to reduce memory churn, but could affect runtime slices.

cheng: I'm starting a bisect across the merge set. steps:
1) checkout release/v1.8
2) git bisect start --bad 1.8.3-merge-4821 --good 1.8.2
3) run perf/ci/run_single.sh --profile long-ctx
4) record throughput.

marta: ping me when you have a culprit commit, I'll prepare a hotpatch branch and QA run.

ci-bot: starting bisect job (queued on perf runners). ETA ~12m.

(small pause)

cheng: quick update — bisect points to commit 8f3c1a9: "runtime: prefer fused-attn on midseq when batch>6"

omar: can we reproduce locally with a minimal harness?

cheng: yes, patching that commit out restores throughput to ~90 tok/s in my run. KV cache tail latency also drops.

anya: so kernel preference change is the culprit. two options: revert commit 8f3c1a9 on release/v1.8 or backport a fix that keeps previous selector for seq>=512.

marta: prefer minimal blast radius — cherry-pick a revert to release branch as hotpatch, then test. If stable, push a canary deploy.

omar: agreed. @release-bot can you open a hotpatch PR and kick off the backport CI?

release-bot: created PR #4890: "hotpatch(release/v1.8): revert runtime kernel preference change (8f3c1a9)". CI: started. Link: https://ci.example.com/pr/4890

ci-bot: backport CI: unit tests OK, perf sanity run queued.

cheng: also adding a small regression test to perf harness that asserts kernel-switches per token < 0.5 for long-ctx baseline. will attach to PR.

marta: test plan for verification:
- run 3 independent perf runs on canary (fresh runners)
- compare median throughput to baseline (1.8.2)
- check KV cache hit & tail p99 latency
- smoke LLM QA on a few prompts

omar: rollout plan: if canary passes, promote to 10% traffic -> 30% -> 100% with 15m hold each and automated rollback if throughput drops >5%.

anya: leave the heuristic change for a proper follow-up — we should re-evaluate selector cost model with real kernel timings. I can instrument and collect microbenchmarks next week.

cheng: re: cherry-pick commands I'm using: 
```
git checkout -b hotfix/revert-kernelpref release/v1.8
git revert --no-commit 8f3c1a9
git commit -m "hotpatch: revert kernel pref that regressed perf"
git push origin hotfix/revert-kernelpref
```

marta: QA run scheduled in 30m. tagging @sre for deployment window.

omar: thanks all. keep notes in the PR. if canary fails, we'll revert the revert and try alternate mapping that avoids the extra kernel switches.

sylvia: noted. also documenting this case in eng-runtime/knowledge base: kernel-selector regressions and how batching heuristics can surface them.

ci-bot: perf sanity for PR #4890: throughput 89 tok/s (baseline 88) — passes.

release-bot: PR merged to release/v1.8 and hotpatch image published: gcr.io/redwood/release:v1.8.3-hotfix-4890

marta: canary deployed (10%). monitoring dashboards show throughput +3% vs baseline. holding 15m.

omar: closing loop: we'll ship follow-up change with improved cost model and add perf regression guard for kernel-switch metric. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
